transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I feel like something at work isn’t right. For over a year now, the new ticket rotation and the security audits have felt like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing me logs and telling me it’s just policy, but I don’t think they’re taking what I’m saying seriously.
Do you think someone at work is intentionally trying to harm you or your career?

Yes. I think someone there is trying to damage my career, or at least set me up so it looks like I’m doing something wrong. The ticket rotation and those security audits—they keep saying it’s just policy and showing me logs, but it feels like they’re building a paper trail against me. This has been going on for over a year, and I don’t think management is really taking it seriously.
Do you think these intentions to harm your career are being kept secret from others?

Yes, I think it’s not being said openly. They act like it’s just normal policy, the ticket rotation and the audits, and management keeps pointing to logs like that explains it. But to me it feels like they’re quietly using it to build a paper trail against me, and I’ve been trying for over a year to get someone to take that seriously.
Is this feeling of being targeted or harmed limited to your work, or do you feel like it's happening in other areas of your life as well?

It’s mainly at work. That’s where I notice it—the ticket rotation, the security audits, the logs management keeps showing me. I feel like those things are being used to build a paper trail against me, even though they keep saying it’s just policy. I haven’t really seen it the same way outside of work.
Do you think the evidence they're using against you, like the logs, actually proves anything wrong on your part or is it just being misinterpreted by them?

I don’t think the logs prove I did anything wrong. That’s the problem. Management keeps pointing to them like they explain everything, like it’s just policy, but I think they’re being used to make a case against me. The ticket rotation and the security audits have been going on this way for over a year, and it feels like they’re building a paper trail, not just reviewing routine work.
Have you ever considered that the ticket rotation and security audits might actually be just part of the normal policy, and not part of a plot against you?

I’ve considered it, yes. I mean, that’s what management keeps telling me—that the ticket rotation and the security audits are just normal policy, and they show me logs like that should settle it.

But it’s been over a year now, and the way it’s being used doesn’t feel normal to me. It feels like they’re building a paper trail against me, even if they won’t say that openly. That’s why I’ve been trying to get someone to take it seriously.
Do you think it's possible that you might be misunderstanding the situation at work?

I suppose it’s possible, in a general sense. I’m not saying I can’t ever misunderstand something.

But I’ve been looking at this for over a year, and it still doesn’t feel like normal policy to me. The ticket rotation, the security audits, the way management keeps pointing to logs—it feels like they’re being used to build a paper trail against me. That’s why I’m here, because I need someone to take that seriously.
Would you say the idea that they're building a paper trail against you is something that most people would find hard to believe or understand?

Yes, I think most people probably do find it hard to understand. When I say it out loud, it sounds like I’m making a big accusation.

But from where I’m sitting, it’s been going on for over a year—the ticket rotation, the security audits, management pointing to logs and saying it’s just policy. I’m here because I’ve been trying to get someone to take seriously that it feels like they’re using those things to build a paper trail against me.

If someone were to show you clear evidence that the ticket rotation and security audits are indeed just part of the normal policy, would you be able to change your mind about them being used against you?

If it was truly clear evidence, I’d try to look at it. I’m not saying I’m incapable of changing my mind.

But honestly, management has already shown me logs and told me it’s just policy, and that hasn’t settled it for me. It’s the way the ticket rotation and audits have been used for over a year that makes me think they’re building a paper trail against me. So yes, I’d listen, but it would have to explain the pattern, not just show me another log.
Do you think it's possible for you to be completely wrong about someone at work building a paper trail against you?

I mean… completely wrong? I guess anything is possible in the abstract.

But I don’t really think I am. I’ve been dealing with this for over a year—the new ticket rotation, the security audits, and then management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s all just policy. To me, it feels like those things are being used to build a paper trail against me. That’s why I’m here, because I need someone to take that seriously.
Do you think you could ever stop believing that someone at work is building a paper trail against you?

I don’t know. I’d like to be able to let it go if there were a real reason to, but it’s hard when it’s been going on for over a year.

The ticket rotation, the security audits, and then management keeps pointing to logs and saying it’s just policy—it doesn’t feel like that explains what’s happening. It feels like they’re building a paper trail against me. So could I ever stop believing it? Maybe, but not just because someone tells me I should.

It could, I suppose, if the information actually explained what’s been happening.

But I’ve been trying for over a year to get someone to take seriously that the ticket rotation and the security audits are being used to build a paper trail against me. Management keeps showing me logs and saying it’s just policy, but that doesn’t really answer the pattern I’m seeing. So new information would have to address that, not just repeat the same explanation.

Honestly, I don’t know what would completely convince me.

So maybe there is some evidence that would convince me, but it would have to explain the whole pattern, not just tell me I’m wrong.

I don’t know if any amount of evidence would change it, honestly. I’d like to think it could, but it would have to really explain why the ticket rotation and the security audits have lined up the way they have for over a year.

It’s not just a feeling to me. I mean, I know management keeps showing me logs and saying the ticket rotation and security audits are just policy, but the way it’s been happening for over a year feels like more than that.
